_comment: Gate B3 floors every tap target at 88px on its short edge, so BrandButton lifts anything shorter; the heights here are written at that floor rather than under it. EVERYTHING the maths tutorial looks and feels like. This file is the UI/UX surface: a designer retunes the whole tutorial without opening a .gd. `roles` maps each drawn part to a palette role in data/themes/theme_*.json, so a reskin is a role swap, not a code change. `layout` is pixels, `pacing` is milliseconds, `visual` is the geometry of the drawn representations.

layout._comment: Retuned after reading all 164 rendered cards, not from the numbers: Skip outweighed the title, every picture floated in a band it never filled, and two-line bodies sat hard against the nav row. Budgeted against the 960x540 design viewport in project.godot: 40 padding + 88 header + 12 dots + 140 visual + 52 body + 88 nav + 4 separations leaves the board inside the screen with the Gate B3 tap-target floor intact on both button rows. Grow visual_height or body_min_h and the nav row walks off the bottom.

_brief_cards_comment: Which authored cards a BRIEF lesson plays. A brief lesson is what a child gets for a new rung inside a domain they have already been taught -- see role of TutorialManager.depth_for(). Names match the `body` field of a card in data/curriculum/tutorials.json; every lesson is authored as see/model/worked/try. The pair here is the picture that carries the strategy and the equation with the reasoning said out loud, which is the shortest thing that still answers 'how do I do this one'. Dropping `try` is deliberate: a guided question in front of the owl's real question is two questions to answer one owl. Naming a card that does not exist falls the lesson back to all four rather than opening on nothing.

pacing._comment: Nothing auto-advances. A child sets the pace; the only timers are the ones that hold a moment long enough to be read.

roles._comment: Left side: what the tutorial draws. Right side: a palette role every theme already defines. Remap freely, but token_a and token_b must clear 3:1 against the board in all seven palettes -- test_theme_roles.gd fails the build otherwise. There is deliberately no token_c: the pattern strip used to need a third colour and NO role in these palettes is both legible on the board and distinct from the other two everywhere, so the repeat is carried by SHAPE now (circle, square, diamond) and colour only reinforces it.
roles.title: accent
